section_summary: This section contains the concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly political report for February 1939 (Despatch No. 3742), internal State Department records regarding the report for March 1939, and the complete text and transmission covers of the March 1939 monthly political report (Despatch No. 3826). The reports analyze Japan's evolving foreign relations with the United States, Great Britain, France, and the Soviet Union, ongoing military campaigns and trade restrictions in China, the annexation of the Spratly Islands, and the signing of the Italo-Japanese Cultural Agreement. They also detail Japanese domestic politics, notably the proceedings of the 74th 'Asia Promotion' Diet, record wartime budgets, price control mechanisms, and economic mobilization laws, accompanied by comprehensive registers of diplomatic despatches and telegrams sent to Washington.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of the Tokyo Embassy's monthly political report reviewing Japan's external relations, domestic politics, legislation, finance, and diplomatic transmissions for February 1939.
subfiles.summary: This document forms the concluding section of the Embassy's February 1939 monthly political report (Despatch No. 3742). It covers French diplomatic representations concerning Japan's occupation of Hainan Island, the deadlocked Soviet-Japanese negotiations over Siberian fisheries, Katsuji Debuchi's interpellation in the House of Peers regarding foreign perceptions of Japan's government, and the aborted merger between the Social Mass Party and Tohokai. It further reports on Diet debates over administrative bureaucracy and economic controls, the presentation of the 1939–40 budget, soaring raw silk prices and price-capping measures, and proposed welfare ordinances limiting industrial working hours. The report concludes with detailed registers of despatches (Nos. 3647–3712) and telegrams (Nos. 63–114) sent to the State Department during February 1939.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of February, 1939 (Despatch No. 3742)

subfiles.summary: Transmitted under covering Despatch No. 3826 by Ambassador Joseph C. Grew, this monthly political report (Report No. 150) provides an extensive review of conditions in Japan during March 1939. It chronicles major American diplomatic protests against sweeping trade and exchange controls in North China and the recurrent bombing of American properties and missions by Japanese aircraft, which were temporarily softened by public Japanese gratitude for the return of late Ambassador Hiroshi Saito's ashes aboard the USS Astoria. The report examines bitter Anglo-Japanese frictions over the British £10,000,000 stabilization loan to China, major Japanese military offensives capturing Nanchang and Wuning, the formal annexation of the Spratly Islands under the Government General of Formosa, and the signing of the Italo-Japanese Cultural Agreement. Finally, it analyzes the adjournment of the 74th 'Asia Promotion' Diet after passing unprecedented budgets exceeding nine billion yen, the six-year Fourth Naval Replenishment Program, and lists of despatches sent to the State Department during March.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3826 with Enclosure No. 1 (Report No. 150): Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of March, 1939
